newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH FINMIN SETS CZK2.8BLN FLOOD BOND ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH FINMIN SETS CZK2.8BLN FLOOD BOND ISSUE.

text.p: The Czech Finance Ministry said on Friday it had set a third issue of flood bonds for August 29 with a total nominal value of 2.8 billion crowns.
It said the deadline for its second flood bond issue, of 1.2 billion crowns, had been brought forward to the same date, August 29.
Foreigners will be allowed to participate in both issues.
"In contrast with the first issue, both of these issues are to be available for sale not only to locals but also to foreigners," the Finance Ministry statement said.
Conditions for all three five-year flood bond issues are the same, except that the third issue will be made in book-entry form.

The first tranche of five-year bonds was issued with a fixed rate of 12.5 percent for the first year. The final four years of maturity would have an interest rate equal to the average inflation rate for the previous 12 months plus 250 basis points.
Severe flooding last month devastated parts of eastern Czech Republic. Economists have estimated the cost at 50-100 billion crowns ($2.9 billion).
-- Robin Shepherd, Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003 ($ = 34.34 Czech Crowns)
